wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: IAM roles' policies can be managed through IAM APIs and do not require root for ordinary changes.

items.prompt: IAM last-accessed information shows that a role used Amazon S3 during the review period. The team wants to remove all S3 actions except the one used by the role. What additional evidence is needed?
constraints: The report does not identify every object-level action used by the workload.
The role has an incident-recovery path not exercised in the review period.
The team can inspect CloudTrail data events and test the documented paths.

options.text: Identify the exact actions, resources, and infrequent recovery operations from audit evidence and workload documentation before removing S3 permissions.
Remove every S3 action except the most recently observed one because service-level use proves the rest are unused.
Grant administrator access during the rollout so the role can recover if the narrowed policy fails.
Ignore the report because last-accessed information cannot inform least-privilege work at all.

feedback.Reason: Service-level last-accessed evidence does not prove that every unused action or resource can be removed safely, especially for unobserved recovery paths.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: IAM last-accessed information helps identify services or actions used during an observation period, but permission refinement still requires action/resource detail and complete workload knowledge. CloudTrail data events can add object-level evidence for supported services.
Details.scenarioApplication: The team should map the recovery path, inspect the relevant data events, test the proposed policy, and remove only permissions proven unnecessary.
Details.errorCorrection: A recent service use does not identify the complete required action set, while administrator access masks the policy under review and ignoring all evidence wastes a useful diagnostic signal.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Least privilege is iterative: keeping unused access has security cost, but removing a recovery permission without evidence has availability cost.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Service-level use does not prove that only the most recently observed action is required.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Administrator access invalidates the least-privilege rollout test and expands incident impact.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Last-accessed data is useful evidence, but it must be combined with workload and audit context.

items.prompt: A bucket policy names a specific assumed-role session principal, but a new session name from the same role is denied. What is the most likely policy-design issue?
constraints: The role permissions policy allows the object action.
The bucket is in the same account.
The role itself is approved, but session names are intentionally generated per run.

options.text: The resource policy is tied to one role session rather than the stable role principal; use the appropriate role principal form for the intended access boundary.
The new session must use the old session name because STS role sessions cannot vary their names.
Add root access because resource policies cannot authorize assumed roles.
Make the bucket public because session names are not valid policy principals.

feedback.Reason: A resource policy bound to one role session does not automatically match every later session of the same role.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: IAM distinguishes role ARNs and role-session principals in resource-based policy evaluation. A policy that names a specific session can be narrower than a policy that names the stable role, and the session name is part of the principal identity.
Details.scenarioApplication: The owner should choose the stable role principal if every approved session should access the bucket, or intentionally keep session-specific grants when that is the required boundary.
Details.errorCorrection: STS permits distinct session names, and root or public access are not required to authorize an approved role.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A stable role principal is easier to operate but grants every session of that role; session-specific principals provide tighter scope at the cost of lifecycle complexity.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Role sessions can use different names and are commonly named per run or actor.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Resource policies can authorize roles and role sessions when the principal form matches.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Making the bucket public removes the intended principal boundary and is not necessary.
